reviewer: Claude Code (AI first-pass source audit; not an independent human curator)
scope: 1-based manifest positions 91-100 of data/validation/self_run_p0_candidates.json, frozen order; 10 candidates, 19 arms
blinding: self_run_p0_predictions.json and all model outputs NOT opened. FRDB snapshot (zip SHA256 647b80d9...9c7a verified) was read after dropping every column containing "cmax"; arms were mapped by AUC, t1/2, n, sex, and population/application comments only. Source Cmax values were read from originals only after each arm mapping was fixed. No observed-vs-predicted comparison was made.
method_note: Single AI pass. Accessible originals: PMDA ramosetron CTD 2.7.6 (K105) + review report (A100) + current IF 19th rev (cited _016 404); PMDA garenoxacin review report (A100) + current Geninax IF 9th rev (cited _007 404; printed page matches cited PDF page 41); ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 results for NCT04427917. Journal originals for PHA-543613 (DMD), pericyazine and carbazochrome (Elsevier), ragaglitazar and polythiazide (Wiley), fenspiride (T&F, Springer) and cifenline (J Pharm Sci) are closed-access (OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar/Europe PMC: no OA copy; publisher 403) and were time-boxed to PubMed abstracts. No browser automation, no account-requiring service, no user email sent. IR is not inferred from route; conventional tablets/capsules not worded IR are verified_with_caveat, following the 81-90 convention.
unresolved_issues: Carbazochrome (577): the source dosed and measured carbazochrome sodium SULFONATE, not carbazochrome/carbazochrome salicylate (the manifest SMILES has no sulfonate). Ruled ineligible on analyte identity; the coordinator should confirm the FRDB compound-to-analyte mapping error.
PF-06835919 (59653): dosed about 20 min before breakfast (Day 1 of QD x7) -> ruled ineligible; the FRDB FASTED label is contradicted by the registry.
Fenspiride (3277): both arms are modified/slow-release per the abstracts -> ineligible. Full texts were not seen.

Garenoxacin (437): 61001 fasting for all 4 doses is explicit in IF_009 p.18 and PMC3249185 Table 1 (per coordinator locators); 100/200/600 mg are above/below the approved 400 mg dose. AI464007 (frdb_1025) Cmax is a geometric mean and its formulation is unspecified.
Ramosetron (1835): doses are the hydrochloride salt (5 µg); conventional film-coated tablets.

Paywalled originals needing library retrieval: Shaffer 2007 DMD (PHA-543613: dose vehicle, fasting, parent vs radioactivity, CYP2D6 PM subject in the per-sex n=4 mean), Cai 2017 JPBA (pericyazine: fasting/product), Skrumsager 2003 JCP (ragaglitazar 120 mg table), Hobbs 1978 CPT (polythiazide), Massarella 1986 J Pharm Sci (cifenline: which oral product maps to the FRDB arm).

arms.reason: Shaffer et al., Drug Metab Dispos 2007;35:1188-95 ([3H]PHA-543613 human ADME study, 4 M + 4 F white healthy subjects). Original is paywalled/closed (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and Europe PMC report no OA copy; publisher site returned 403 to non-browser fetch); time-boxed. Only the PubMed abstract was read. The abstract confirms a single oral dose of [3H]1 in humans but gives no dose, formulation (solution vs capsule), fasting state, or Cmax table; the FRDB male arm (n=4, AUC0-12 per FRDB) could not be matched to a table. Extra caveat: one of 8 subjects was a probable CYP2D6 poor metabolizer with disparate exposure, which may be inside the per-sex mean (n=4). Plasma unchanged-parent vs total-radioactivity Cmax is also unconfirmed.

arms.formulation_evidence: not accessible (radiolabeled oral dose; vehicle unknown)

arms.reason: Hu et al., J Chromatogr B 2014;951-952:1-6. The abstract states the analyte and dosed drug are carbazochrome sodium SULFONATE (CSS; MRM m/z 299.0->256.0 = carbazochrome sulfonate anion), given as a '90mg CSS formulation' to 18 healthy Chinese males under fasting conditions. CSS is a different molecular entity (a sulfonic-acid derivative, C10H11N4NaO5S) from the manifest parent SMILES (carbazochrome, no sulfonate) and from carbazochrome salicylate. The analyte/dosed parent does not match the frozen candidate structure, so this arm is ineligible. The full text is paywalled (Elsevier), so the formulation (tablet type) and Cmax table were not seen.

arms.dose_evidence: 90 mg CSS (sodium sulfonate salt), not carbazochrome
arms.uncertainty: low for the ineligibility call (analyte identity is explicit in the abstract)

arms.reason: Skrumsager et al., J Clin Pharmacol 2003;43:1244-56. Original is paywalled/closed (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and Europe PMC report no OA copy; publisher site returned 403 to non-browser fetch); time-boxed. Only the PubMed abstract was read. The abstract confirms single oral doses of 1-120 mg in healthy subjects, rapid absorption (tmax 1.5-1.7 h), and dose-proportional Cmax. It does not confirm the 120 mg group size (FRDB n=6), fasting state, formulation, statistic, or the table value.
arms.dose_evidence: 120 mg is within the abstract's 1-120 mg single-dose range

arms.reason: Hobbs & Twomey, Clin Pharmacol Ther 1978;23:241-6. Original is paywalled/closed (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and Europe PMC report no OA copy; publisher site returned 403 to non-browser fetch); time-boxed. Only the PubMed abstract was read. The abstract confirms single 1 mg oral doses in 'normal human subjects', with plasma polythiazide measured by electron-capture GC (hydrolysis to trifluoroethylthioacetaldehyde; LOQ 0.2 ng/mL) and elimination t1/2 25.7 h (matches FRDB). It does not state n, fasting, formulation (Renese tablet presumed), or Cmax statistic. Caveat: the hydrolysis-based assay may not fully distinguish parent from any hydrolysable species.
arms.population: normal subjects, M/F (MeSH ages adolescent-middle aged; FRDB FEMALE / MALE)

arms.reason: Medvedovici et al., Bioanalysis 2011;3:1935-47. The abstract states the BE studies used 'a modified release pharmaceutical formulation containing 80 mg fenspiride hydrochloride' (fasting and fed single-dose arms). A modified-release formulation is ineligible under the IR-only rule. The full text was not accessed (T&F 403), and fasting vs fed mapping of the FRDB arm (n=15, AUC per FRDB) is moot.
arms.fasting_evidence: fasting and fed arms exist; mapping unconfirmed
arms.formulation_evidence: 'modified release pharmaceutical formulation containing 80 mg fenspiride hydrochloride'

arms.reason: Montes et al., Eur J Clin Pharmacol 1993;45:169-72 (12 healthy males, crossover 80 mg fenspiride HCl IV vs oral tablet). The abstract says 'The tablet had slow release characteristics', with oral Tmax 6 h. The oral product is therefore not immediate release, and the arm is ineligible. FRDB AUC (n=12, t1/2 16 h) is consistent with the oral arm. Full text paywalled (Springer auth redirect); fasting not confirmed.
arms.uncertainty: low-moderate: the ineligibility rests on the authors' own 'slow release' wording

arms.reason: Overseas food-effect study AI464007, fasted arm (reference data): 13 evaluable healthy adults (13 M + 1 F enrolled, 1 dropout). A100 p.27 (printed 26) table AUC 71.7 µg·h/mL matches FRDB (Non-Japanese, n=13). Caveats: (1) the reported Cmax is a GEOMETRIC mean, not arithmetic; (2) the formulation used in AI464007 is not specified in A100 (the other overseas studies used capsules); (3) the review report is secondary to the sponsor study report.

arms.reason: NCT04427917 (Pfizer phase 1 multiple-dose study in healthy Japanese adults; ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 results). The FRDB arm is Day 1 (first dose) of 300 mg QD x 7 days, n=6. The results group description says dosing was 'approximately 20 minutes prior to the start of breakfast on Days 1-7'. A meal starting 20 min post-dose, before the median Tmax of 0.834 h, is not a fasted single dose, so the arm is ineligible despite the FRDB FASTED label. The Day 1 Cmax is also a geometric mean (CV%), and the regimen is multiple-dose (Day 1 = first dose). Formulation is not specified in the registry.
arms.exact_locator: Results > Outcome Measures 'Summary of Maximum Plasma Concentration (Cmax) of PF-06835919 on Day 1 and Day 7', Day 1 row
arms.fasting_evidence: 'approximately 20 minutes prior to the start of breakfast' -> not fasted

arms.reason: Massarella, Silvestri & Lin, J Pharm Sci 1986;75:894-6. Original is paywalled/closed (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and Europe PMC report no OA copy; publisher site returned 403 to non-browser fetch); time-boxed. Only the PubMed abstract was read. The abstract confirms 18 healthy adults in an open 4-way crossover: 160 mg cibenzoline capsule, tablet, oral solution, and IV infusion. Plasma cibenzoline was measured by HPLC. The single FRDB arm (n=18, AUC per FRDB, t1/2 7.8 h) cannot be mapped to a specific oral product (capsule, tablet or solution) without the tables. Fasting state and salt basis (cibenzoline succinate vs base) are also unconfirmed. All three oral forms would be IR, so eligibility is likely, but the arm mapping and fasting are unverified.
arms.formulation_evidence: capsule, tablet and oral solution arms exist; FRDB arm-to-product mapping unknown

coordinator_review: Codex second-pass adjudication, predictions and FRDB Cmax kept sealed. PMDA K105 establishes ramosetron fasted parent-plasma Cmax after conventional film-coated 5 µg tablets. Current PMDA-linked garenoxacin IF _009 plus PMDA A100 establish the Japanese fasted conventional tablet/capsule cohorts. PMDA English review https://www.pmda.go.jp/files/000153135.pdf pp.32-33 further establishes that foreign AI464007 fasted arm frdb_1025 used two 200 mg tablets; its Cmax is a geometric mean. Conventional tablet/capsule with no modified-release design is treated as immediate release. Fenspiride modified/slow-release, carbazochrome chemical mismatch, and PF-06835919 pre-breakfast dose remain ineligible; abstract-only sources remain unverified.
